canonical_statement: For centered jointly Gaussian real vectors X and Y on a common nonempty finite index type, possibly on different probability spaces, equal coordinate variances and Cov(X_i,X_j) <= Cov(Y_i,Y_j) for distinct indices imply P(for all i, X_i <= t) <= P(for all i, Y_i <= t) for every real t.
domain_and_universes: universes u v w; nonempty finite I : Type u; measurable ΩX : Type v and ΩY : Type w; measures μX and μY; random vectors X : ΩX -> I -> Real and Y : ΩY -> I -> Real
ordered_binders: ΩX : Type v, [MeasurableSpace ΩX], μX : Measure ΩX
ΩY : Type w, [MeasurableSpace ΩY], μY : Measure ΩY
X : ΩX -> I -> Real, Y : ΩY -> I -> Real
hypotheses: HasGaussianLaw X μX and HasGaussianLaw Y μY
off-diagonal covariance of X is at most that of Y
conclusion: For every t : Real, μX {ω | forall i, X ω i <= t} <= μY {ω | forall i, Y ω i <= t}.

killed: changed random-vector probability domain to deterministic vectors
moved threshold before hypotheses and discarded substantive assumptions

degenerate_cases: The index type is nonempty. No covariance nonsingularity, positive variance, coordinate distinctness, common sample space, or density assumption is imposed. The singleton-index event is kernel-checked.
status_boundary: Statement-only evidence. Primary-source audit, proof, trust closure, hermetic replay, and independent acceptance remain downstream.
